purpose: Audit whether X-IIoTID contains enough temporal support to forecast progression from observable early malicious stages to exploitation-or-later activity, before training any progression model.

stage_semantics.boundary: Exploitation or later is treated as the progression/compromise-side boundary for this development audit. Reconnaissance and Weaponisation are observable malicious precursors, not compromise.

temporal_protocol.entity: source IP when present, otherwise GLOBAL
temporal_protocol.eligible_history: all eight history minutes contain only benign or early-pre-compromise stages
temporal_protocol.observed_early_history_subset: eligible history with at least one Reconnaissance/Weaponisation stage in the eight-minute history
temporal_protocol.positive_target: future four minutes contain at least one Exploitation-or-later stage
temporal_protocol.negative_target: future four minutes contain only benign or early-pre-compromise stages
temporal_protocol.unknown_or_unmapped_stage_rule: skip the sequence rather than force a label
temporal_protocol.lead_time: for positive sequences, seconds from history cutoff to first Exploitation-or-later stage in the future horizon

split_protocol.purpose: support audit only; report observed-early positive/negative support in every partition

claim_boundary: A V40 pass only establishes that X-IIoTID has enough development support for an early-stage-to-later-stage progression experiment. It is not forecasting accuracy, not a final pre-compromise claim, and not a production containment approval.
final_validation: locked; X-IIoTID has already informed earlier development, so any later V41/V42 model selected here requires a newly reserved external dataset or controlled campaign for final claims
